source.title: Inference-Time Decomposition of Activations (ITDA): A Scalable Approach to Interpreting Large Language Models
source.authors: Patrick Leask; Neel Nanda; N. A. Moubayed

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests representational similarity across independently initialized model instances and across training checkpoints using ITDA dictionary Jaccard similarity, a different measure from the original convergence studies.
record.gate_note: The representation-similarity experiments in Sections 5 and A.4 bear on convergence. Reconstruction and interpretability comparisons do not bear on the claim. The layer-similarity heatmaps contain many figure-only cell values; those are not separately extracted. The paper does not test cross-modal alignment or whether alignment rises with capability.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper on ITDA, a cheap alternative to SAEs. Its similarity section uses the Kornblith layer-matching benchmark. That benchmark assumes corresponding layers of different-seed GPT-2 instances are most similar, and scores metrics against that assumption. The accuracies (r1–r10) therefore rate the metrics, not whether convergence holds. The model-level Jaccard values (r11–r12) are offered as validation that dictionaries 'track the difference between the models.' The Pythia checkpoint experiment (r13–r18) compares one model with its own final checkpoint, not independently trained models. No result is set up to show whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that ITDA is a far cheaper SAE alternative (about 100x faster, about 1% of tokens) with interpretable atom labels. They show it scales to Llama 3.1 70B and 405B, but it reconstructs worse than TopK and similar SAEs. Its dictionary Jaccard index is state-of-the-art on layer matching. The Pythia checkpoint result is presented as reproducing Raghu et al., with early layers converging first.
record.recipe_differences: Uses dictionaries of sampled model activations and Jaccard overlap of their prompt-token labels, rather than the original studies' representation-comparison procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer-matching accuracy varies by similarity measure. The authors also report convergence for the first two layers but not for other layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia 70m, 160m and 410m, ITDA similarity to the final checkpoint reaches 1 in the last third of training for the first two layers only. Later layers do not converge (Fig. 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a single model, early layers' representations stabilize earlier in training than later layers.

fits_no_version.finding: On the Kornblith layer-matching benchmark across five GPT-2 seeds, metrics differ widely. Accuracy ranges from 0.07–0.16 (linear regression) to 0.88–0.89 (ITDA).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similarity metrics differ greatly in how well they recover layer correspondence across seeds (a metric-quality benchmark).

fits_no_version.finding: Jaccard overlap of unioned ITDA dictionaries is higher within an architecture (0.56–0.59) than between GPT-2 small and medium (0.46–0.47).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ITDA dictionary overlap can discriminate model architectures, which may be useful for model diffing.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The similarity evidence is limited to GPT-2 instance comparisons and Pythia checkpoint comparisons. The paper provides no uncertainty estimates for the reported scores. Some layer-wise similarity results are presented only in heatmaps, and the paper notes that specific layer comparisons vary.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5.1 Figures 2 and A.4 contain layer-by-layer heatmaps averaged across model pairs. Their many individual figure-only cell values were not extracted; the table's layer-matching accuracies and the text-described training outcomes are recorded instead.

untested.parts: No sweep across architectures, objectives or data relating alignment to scale or capability.
Correspondence across seeds is assumed by the benchmark rather than tested. No measure of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability test.
No cross-model comparison of features or circuits.
Metrics are ranked on a benchmark. There is no test of whether measured convergence shifts with metric settings, inputs or OOD data.
No test of whether alignment is complete or plateaus across models, and none of shared data or objectives as causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V3, V6 and V7 links are overturned. The layer-matching task presupposes convergence across seeds in order to score metrics. The Pythia experiment is within-model, not across independently trained models. Table 1 is mislabelled 'Table 2' in the paper's text.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep testing whether alignment rises with model size and capability across different architectures, objectives, or data.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language comparison.
Measures layer matching and dictionary overlap, not whether the same individual features or shared subspaces are learned.
No test of mapping one model's representations onto another's, stitching, or interchangeability.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Compares similarity metrics on layer matching; does not test changes from metric settings, neighbour counts, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete similarity and layer-specific training convergence, but does not test whether shared data or objectives cause the overlap.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small and GPT-2 medium instances
rows.operation_detail: Compared unioned ITDA dictionaries across different instances of the same architecture using Jaccard similarity.
rows.note: The paper reports a range across different instances of either architecture, not separate values for each architecture.
rows.check: Jaccard overlap of greedily built prompt-token dictionaries. It depends on the threshold τ and on sampling, and no reference for full alignment is given. The authors use it to validate model differencing, not to test convergence. The 0.56–0.59 value cannot be read as a degree of feature sharing.

rows.value: similarity converges to 1 during the last third of training

rows.check: Measures within-model stability across training checkpoints against the final checkpoint. These are not independently trained models, so the row does not bear on V7 or any other version.

relation.reason: Section 5.1 assumes corresponding layers across initializations should be most similar and scores metrics against that expectation. Section 5.2 validates dictionary-based discrimination rather than independently testing a claim version.

tranche.reason: The experiments evaluate ITDA as an interpretability and similarity method. Layer correspondence and architecture discrimination serve as benchmarks; checkpoint stabilization measures a different construct from the catalog claims.

source_check.notes: Rows r1–r10 report similarity-method benchmark performance, not convergence strength. Rows r13–r18 accurately reproduce checkpoint results but require cannot_determine for the catalog claims.
